# Ratify Labs

> Open reference implementations showing how a receiver verifies delegated authority before an AI agent acts.

Ratify Labs is the canonical catalog for runnable labs and open reference pages
about receiver-owned authorization. A classifier, model, agent framework, or
network credential may propose or carry a request; the receiver checks the
signed delegation, scope, resource, operation, freshness, expiry, and local
policy before the protected action runs.

## Start here

- [Ratify Labs catalog](https://labs.ratifyprotocol.com/): browse every hosted lab and open reference.
- [Maritime authorization lab](https://labs.ratifyprotocol.com/maritime/): run allow, limit, resource, expiry, revocation, replay, and agent-isolation checks.
- [classifier.dev authorization lab](https://labs.ratifyprotocol.com/classifier-dev/): compare semantic classification with exact delegated authority.

## Open references

- [GitHub Copilot](https://labs.ratifyprotocol.com/copilot): verify an exact deployment action over MCP.
- [Google ADK](https://labs.ratifyprotocol.com/google-adk): verify a multi-agent handoff across separately anchored domains.
- [LangChain](https://labs.ratifyprotocol.com/langchain): verify an exact MCP action without giving the model the signing key.
- [NVIDIA OpenShell plus NOOA](https://labs.ratifyprotocol.com/nvidia-openshell-nooa): verify a bounded cross-company order action.
- [Ratify Edge Physical AI](https://labs.ratifyprotocol.com/edge-sentinel): verify an edge action before an actuator runs.

## Source and protocol

- [Labs catalog source](https://github.com/identities-ai/ratify-labs)
- [Ratify Protocol](https://github.com/identities-ai/ratify-protocol)
- [Ratify Protocol documentation](https://docs.ratifyprotocol.com)

Each reference page identifies its canonical source, prerequisites, run command,
evidence, limitations, and whether it is a hosted lab or a reference to run
locally. Platform names indicate implementation context, not endorsement or
partnership.
